market_context.summary: A rates and inflation shock, not a growth scare. Equities fell a fourth straight session on 2026-09-10 with the 10-year Treasury yield above 4.95%, its highest since October 2023, and the 2-year up 15.2bp to 4.579%. Long bonds, gold and equities fell together, which is the signature of a term-premium repricing rather than an equity-specific risk-off: real yields rising beats the haven bid, which is why GLD fell 1.73% alongside TLT. The driver behind it is physical — the Strait of Hormuz is effectively closed, Gulf regional exports are down 2.1 mb/d to 15 mb/d, CENTCOM destroyed five Iranian tankers on 2026-09-08, and Brent closed $101.21 on 2026-09-09. Kalshi now prices a 61% chance of a 25bp Fed HIKE on 2026-09-16, up 6 points in one session, with October at 68% hold — one hike priced, not a cycle. The energy tape is discriminating correctly rather than buying the theme wholesale: on 09-10 crude proxy USO rose 5.61% while XLE fell 0.58%, producers and tankers rose, and services fell 2-3%. Aug CPI at 08:30 ET today is the near-term resolution for most of this.

recommendations.thesis: This is an update and nothing about it changes today. The short is 1.0% from its 750 target after four consecutive down sessions, and the driver that put it there is intact: the 10-year above 4.95% is the highest since October 2023 and equity multiples are compressing against it. SPY closed 757.83, below its sma20 of 767.56 and sitting on its sma50 of 758.25.
recommendations.key_risk: The August CPI print at 08:30 ET today is a two-sided event on a position that is already most of the way to its target. Consensus is core easing to 2.4% YoY, and a soft core reading unwinds the 61% September hike probability and squeezes equities straight back through the 767.56 sma20. RED TEAM adds a second dated risk inside the horizon that the idea did not name: 2026-09-18 is September quarterly triple witching and the S&P index rebalance, a mechanical flow event one week out that can move the index against a short independently of rates or CPI.
recommendations.counter_argument: Holding a short 1% from target through a scheduled macro print gives back most of the remaining edge for the rest of the move. The disciplined alternative is covering into the print rather than holding for the last 1%. RED TEAM, and this is the strongest objection in the report: the 2.19:1 in the validation block describes the trade as it was opened at 773.00, not the decision being made today. From 757.83 the remaining reward to the 750.00 target is 7.83 against 25.67 of risk to the unchanged 783.50 stop — a forward reward-to-risk of 0.30:1. A driftless walk touches 750 first about 77% of the time from here, which is exactly what makes the expectancy on holding roughly zero rather than positive: the ratio and the probability cancel. So holding adds no expected value and carries a two-sided macro print in under two hours. Conviction lowered 4 to 3 for that reason. Levels are deliberately left alone — trailing the stop down to bank the gain would manufacture a better-looking ratio without improving the trade, which is the failure mode this report exists to avoid — but the reader should treat covering into the print as at least as defensible as holding.

recommendations.thesis: Brent closed $101.21 on 2026-09-09 after US forces destroyed five Iranian tankers and Houthi strikes hit Saudi facilities, and USO rose 5.61% on 2026-09-10 — yet XLE fell 0.58% that session while Devon rose 2.12% to its highest close in a year. recommendations.key_risk: A negotiated de-escalation in the Gulf takes the geopolitical premium out of crude in days, and E&P equities give back a 5% crude move faster than they earned it. This is also a breakout entry, not a value entry: DVN closed 2026-09-10 at a 52-week closing high and the 55.50 target is 5.3% above the 250-day intraday high of 52.71, so it has not traded there in a year. recommendations.counter_argument: Every geopolitical oil spike since 2022 has mean-reverted within weeks, and buying a producer at a 52-week high after a 5.6% one-day crude move is textbook chasing. The refiners and services names falling on the same day say the market does not believe the move is durable. RED TEAM: conviction lowered 4 to 3. The counter_argument_answered evidence is what lifts this from two independent kinds to three, and it rests entirely on one source that could not be fetched — congress.gov returns 403 to a non-browser request, which is not proof the page is wrong but is proof the claim went unverified — and the form of the source does not match the claim: a numbered CRS background product is the wrong kind of document to carry a 2026-09 export volume. notes.md shows the 2.1 mb/d figure was captured once, from that URL alone, with no second source. Treat the mean-reversion objection as standing rather than answered. The idea itself survives on its own two confirmations: the shelf breakout with a 2.32 ATR stop under both the shelf and the sma20, and measured relative strength against XLE on the same session. Levels unchanged and the arithmetic checks out.

Against the mean-reversion case: this is not a headline spike. Against the chasing case: unlike FRO, which trades 43% above its 200-day average, DVN is only 14% above its own, so the extension here is ordinary rather than parabolic.

data_quality_notes:
RESEARCH RAN TO COMPLETION — notes.md carries a RESEARCH COMPLETE block at 06:30 ET, so `truncated` is false and nothing here is reconstructed. Ten candidate lines resolve to seven distinct ideas (DVN, FRO and SPY were each re-captured once to correct levels or conviction; the last entry per symbol is used). Four are new (DVN, FRO, AAL, DG) and three are position updates (CCJ, SPY, BCC), which are position management rather than new risk.

PRICES. Every level in this report is a 2026-09-10 regular-session close, re-fetched from finnhub at synthesis time with the US market closed (session=pre, age ~870 minutes). At 6am ET that is the freshest honest equity price — a closed market, not stale data. Kalshi contract prices were fetched live at ~06:10 and ~06:23 ET. No price here is estimated.

CONCENTRATION — the most important caveat. Three of the seven ideas are one bet that oil stays high: DVN long a US onshore producer, FRO long a VLCC tanker, AAL short a fuel consumer. That is exactly at the three-idea correlation cap, not over it, but it is a genuine concentration — a negotiated Gulf de-escalation loses on all three simultaneously and they should be sized as one position, not three. XLE was deliberately left un-re-pitched for this reason. DG partially offsets it: management themselves named higher and more volatile fuel prices as their own headwind. A second cluster is rates staying high (SPY short, BCC close), at two.

RATIOS. Recomputed from final levels rather than taken from the notes: DG 2.67 (long-term floor 2.5, measured against a stated $100 bear case), CCJ 4.56, AAL 2.92, SPY 2.19, DVN 2.19, FRO 2.07. DVN and FRO sit close to the 2.0 swing floor and the reader should treat them as the marginal ideas here rather than as comfortably clearing it — though the pattern of targets fitted to the floor is absent: no idea had its stop narrowed to clear a ratio, and stop distances are wide at 2.32 ATR (DVN), 2.74 (FRO), 3.02 (AAL), 2.17 (CCJ) and 1.96 (SPY, against the 1.8 ETF floor). Win probabilities clear the 1/(1+R:R) break-even baseline by 6-17 points, none over the 20-point large-claim line.

THE WEAKEST IDEA, NAMED. FRO is the one to be skeptical of and the research phase said so itself. It closed 2026-09-10 at a 52-week high, +136% off its 250-day low and 43% above its 200-day average, after eight consecutive up sessions, and the 57.50 target is 18% above anything that has traded in a year. It was cut from conviction 4 to 3 and from 2% to 1.5% size for exactly that, and its `counter_argument_answered` evidence entry was removed because the extension objection could not be answered with evidence. This report also already lost money long a tanker — DHT stopped out 2026-08-26. DVN carries the same 52-week-high structure but at 14% above its 200-day rather than 43%.

VENUE. FRO is NYSE-listed ordinary shares (dual-listed NYSE/Oslo Bors, SEC-reporting, files 20-F, CIK 913290), which satisfies config/universe.md. No source was found that explicitly confirms Robinhood offers it, so treat it as listed on an eligible US exchange with app availability not directly verified. All other names are ordinary US-listed equities and ETFs. Liquidity clears the floors everywhere: DVN $524M ADV, AAL $728M, DG $288M, CCJ $276M, FRO $111M. BCC is thinnest at $23M ADV and it is an exit, not an entry.

SOURCES THAT FAILED, ALL MATERIAL. (1) nasdaq short-interest returned ok:false with null fields for every symbol, so NO short-interest or days-to-cover check was possible on any idea — that matters most for the AAL short, where crowding is the main unquantified risk, and it is stated in that idea's key_risk. (2) The yahoo options endpoint returned HTTP 401, so no options-implied-move check was possible on any idea. (3) The yahoo chart API returned 429 throughout: no VIX, no index level, no DXY, and no WTI/Brent futures quote all run, which is why the VIX/DXY/WTI levels above are null and every crude reference is either USO (the ETF) or a sourced Brent print rather than a futures price. (4) finnhub index quotes require a CFD subscription and stooq 404s on index symbols. (5) rbnenergy.com 403s to a non-browser fetch; the $100/bbl diesel crack figure is corroborated against a second source. CoinGecko failed inside the macro call but succeeded via the crypto subcommand.

COVERAGE GAPS. No small or micro caps — every small-cap idea the day's themes pointed at would have been a fourth oil bet, so the gap is recorded rather than padded. No intraday idea: CPI at 08:30 ET is a genuine intraday catalyst, but picking a direction before the print is a coin flip and the conditional version is two ideas pretending to be one. No crypto idea — BTC at 77,104 is drifting with equities rather than bidding on the inflation shock, which is itself informative. No futures idea, since /MCL and /MGC would both be oil bets. The horizon mix (six swing, one long_term, zero intraday) is what survived, not a quota. GLD and SVRA were held unchanged without re-underwriting, and that is the basis for holding them rather than a fresh view. INSW's -2.37% divergence from the other tankers was not resolved. The DG net-sales discrepancy (+0.2% YoY in the transcript against +5.2% in a secondary source) is unresolved and is stated in that idea's counter-argument rather than quietly taking the flattering number; the primary source figure was used.

OPEN BOOK, REPORTED HONESTLY. TLT BUY @82.60 with a stop at 80.95 closed 2026-09-10 at 80.78, BELOW its stop — that position is stopped out on the close, not a hold decision, and no update is pitched for it. The separate TLT SELL exit published 2026-09-02 @81.87 is +1.3% right. NKE and LULU: the exit calls published 2026-09-08 were right and remain right (NKE 36.62 is 0.19% off its 120-day low, LULU 96.88 is 1.26% off its); no re-pitch in either direction, since a falling knife is not a value case and no consumer work was done this run. GLD held with levels unchanged — note the conflict that a GLD SELL @406.77 published 2026-09-08 is still pending above the market alongside the open BUY; neither side was re-pitched because no gold valuation work was done, and the 520 target would not survive an honest bear case anyway (~2.1 R:R against a -14% bear case, under the 2.5 floor).

PENDING ENTRIES. Withdrawals recommended: LCII (about to fill into a falsified thesis — see watchlist), DINO BUY @99.50 (now 107.72, 8.3% above the entry and +94% off its low into a fading crack spread — its whole edge was the entry price), IYR SELL_SHORT @103.60 (now 99.97, i.e. the trade has already travelled its entire intended distance without ever filling). Stale and not re-pitched: BTC SELL @63,400 and /MBTU6 SHORT @64,340 sit ~17% below a spot BTC of 77,104; CEG (+5.1%), VST (+14.9%), EEM (+2.1%) and PFE (+7.2%) all ran away above their entries. REJECTIONS. Fourteen logged with reasons, which is where most of the run's work went: LEN/ITB short and LEN long (both sides of a group already 17-20% off its high at the bottom of its range), OXY, HAL/SLB/OIH, LNG (Cheniere — a six-month-old dislocation the stock is falling through), EQT/AR/RRC (no transmission channel; Henry Hub is down 9% since the closure), the refiner longs VLO/MPC/DINO/PSX/PBF/DK (the group is already up 68-113% off its lows and within 2-4% of its highs as the crack rolls over from $100 to $93), LMT (0.64 R:R against the 2.5 long-term floor), GIS/CAG, KR, MRK/BMY/ABBV/PFE (no de-rating left to buy), AVAV (unresolved accounting and litigation), KTOS, KXFEDDECISION-26SEP-H0, and the whole KXCPIYOY-26AUG ladder (no independent CPI forecast to set against a market distribution already sitting on consensus; it also stops trading at 08:29 ET, roughly two hours after this publishes).
